title: Goal Rush
story: Players explore open roads and score in an unguarded goal before finding a new road.
setup: Create two adjacent 12x15-yard lanes, each with a mini goal at both ends. Put two to four players with a ball in each lane.
instructions: Everyone dribbles at the same time and may score in either goal in their lane.
After scoring, turn away and attack the other goal.
Ask players to look before choosing a goal and shoot when the road opens.
Play 60-second rounds; count personal adventures rather than ranking players.
coach_lens: Look for a final touch out of the feet, a glance toward the goal and a purposeful strike. Avoid prescribing one shooting surface.
questions: What tells you the road to goal is open?
What touch helps you get ready to shoot?

simplify: Widen the goals or shorten the lane.
challenge: Add one roaming blocker who may intercept but not camp in a goal.
low_attendance: Use one lane and keep both goals available.
high_attendance: Add a third lane rather than adding queues.
limited_equipment: Use two-cone gates as goals and retrieve balls after each round.

safety: Keep each lane narrow enough to define space but wide enough to avoid head-on collisions.

diagram.alt: Two side-by-side lanes each have a goal at both ends and players dribbling toward open goals.

source.title: Assess Your Players and Environment - Setting Goals and Objectives
source.reviewer_notes: SmallSide-authored finishing exploration reflecting U.S. Soccer guidance that seven-year-olds need game-like scenarios, frequent involvement, dribbling and shooting. No source wording or artwork reproduced.
